artifact.title: Master Founder & Intellectual Provenance Timeline
artifact.claim_posture: typed chronology synthesis; not independent historical verification

purpose: Reconstruct a single working chronology for the formation of Boundary First Labs and the intellectual development that led into the current Boundary Theory architecture while preserving provenance classes, discontinuities, unresolved transitions, and verification tasks.
governing_rules: Do not create a smooth retrospective story where the record is actually discontinuous.
Do not infer a rename from conceptual similarity.
Separate first use, mature use, and canonical use.
Treat conversation checkpoints as testimony until tied to primary artifacts.
Do not promote autobiographical provenance into scientific validation.
Git dates establish repository presence, not necessarily intellectual first conception.

P.name: Primary / contemporaneous artifact
P.meaning: Dated correspondence, source media, notebooks, Git commits, contemporaneous files, or other direct artifacts.
P.allowed_use: Strongest chronology evidence available internally; substantive claims retain their own claim ceilings.

R.name: Repository-backed synthesis
R.meaning: Current or dated repository document that explicitly reconstructs an earlier period or records current architectural status.
R.allowed_use: Good internal provenance; retrospective claims are not automatically independent verification.

C.name: Conversation / founder checkpoint
C.meaning: Retained dated conversation statement or founder testimony not yet tied to a recovered primary artifact.
C.allowed_use: Preserve chronology and language as testimony; do not upgrade to repository-direct history.

I.name: Interpretive bridge
I.meaning: A synthesis connecting two or more supported milestones.
I.allowed_use: Orientation only; must not manufacture synonymy, causality, or exact transition dates.

OPEN.name: Unresolved
OPEN.meaning: Transition, date, or source remains unresolved.
OPEN.allowed_use: Preserve as a research task rather than filling by inference.

timeline.title: Childhood and adolescence — formative constructive cognition
timeline.summary: Early constructive cognition, repeated encounters with inadequate categories, and a habit of reconstructing the problem rather than assuming offered alternatives were exhaustive. Augusta founder-history adds an educational formation centered on learning, seriousness, capability, character, and excellence.
claims: The mature research program did not begin with a formal theory name.
The founder entered technical education with an existing expectation that difficult learning was legitimate, capability was developable, and authority did not automatically equal understanding.
verification_tasks: Recover primary educational artifacts, dated personal notes, and early technical notebooks relevant to the intellectual chronology.

timeline.title: Technical education and early research formation
timeline.summary: Formal computer-science education spanning AI, systems, and computer architecture; exposure to low-level execution and machine models; and early academic research/publication. Georgia Tech is interpreted as technical intensification rather than absolute origin.
patterns: trace execution rather than trust labels
treat anomalies and null results as information
verification_tasks: Recover exact undergraduate research dates, lab affiliations, papers, projects, and earliest surviving technical notes with clear descendants in later Boundary Theory vocabulary.

timeline.title: Professional software engineering as executable representation laboratory

date.label: exact interval by employer/project to reconstruct

timeline.summary: Software engineering supplied an independent test environment in which representational choices became mechanically consequential. Lean and Agile added a hypothesis-probe-revision discipline that later informed Boundary First and the second-order scientific method.
verification_tasks: Build a project-by-project professional chronology and locate earliest artifacts using boundary, closure, invariant, defect, representation, reconciliation, or hidden-work language.

timeline.title: Long-run GR/QFT comparison problem

date.label: approximately two decades; exact start unresolved

timeline.summary: Repeated attempts to identify common structure between general relativity and quantum field theory exposed incompatibilities among native objects, scale, locality, statistical procedures, and closure conditions, pushing the inquiry toward more primitive representational questions.
generating_questions: How does a local description close?
What survives projection, averaging, coarse-graining, or dimensional reduction?
When do two representations describe the same operative structure?

timeline.title: Attempted external scrutiny of relativistic work
timeline.summary: Origin packet records outreach to Michael Schatz at Georgia Tech Physics and Anthony 'RJ' seeking feedback on an attempted relativistic derivation or extension.
verification_tasks: Recover original messages, attachments, replies, timestamps, and terminology.
constraints: Do not reconstruct exact scientific wording from memory while original correspondence may still be recoverable.

timeline.title: Physical research-room phase
timeline.summary: A dedicated research room functioned as an external cognitive apparatus and manually constructed context window, keeping multiple research branches spatially persistent and mutually inspectable.
verification_tasks: Date photographs and video from metadata and recover corresponding handwritten clusters.

timeline.title: Red Book binder phase

date.label: after research-room expansion; exact dates open

timeline.summary: The research room was compressed into a modular binder supporting insertion, removal, regrouping, and replacement. The fine-structure constant became a major organizing target; the work was then described primarily as dimensional analysis.
verification_tasks: Inventory binder sections, page chronology, inserted/replaced pages, and earliest occurrence of later key mathematical objects.

timeline.title: Continuing pre-AI research corpus
timeline.summary: A substantial corpus of handwritten notes, diagrams, calculations, source papers, code, digital files, research-room media, the Red Book binder, and dated external-criticism attempts existed before generative AI adoption.
timeline.causal_claim: The research direction and corpus predate generative AI; AI later supplied representational throughput for compilation, comparison, expansion, and consolidation.
timeline.claim_ceiling: Provenance only; not proof of mathematical or physical claims.

timeline.title: RGT crystallizes as closure grammar and cross-domain formal spine
timeline.summary: RGT sharpens into a theory of lawful representation change centered on representation, boundaries/interfaces, closure, defects, invariants, and translation.

subevents.description: RGT described as a closure grammar for representational systems and as applying formal-grammar rules to mathematics and systems.
RGT described as a proposed cross-domain formal theory; Representation Context Theory considered as alternate public terminology, with gauge retained as technical machinery.

constraints: Direct primary repository source remains open.

timeline.title: Gauge and closure machinery deepens
timeline.summary: The representation program expands around closure under representation change, invariants, formal grammars, norm/gauge families, n-ball and Gamma recursion, complex phase, transform methods, spectral/operator views, admissibility, and transport.
constraints: The n-ball family is not itself a Distinction Space.

timeline.title: Admissibility Web and explicit Distinction / Emergence differentiation
timeline.summary: An Admissibility Web appears as an intermediate formal object while Distinction Theory and Emergence Theory differentiate into distinct functional roles. Category/type/representation formalization becomes more tractable through an admissibility layer.
timeline.interpretation: Decomposition and refinement of the broader representation program; not yet the current Boundary Theory facet architecture.

timeline.title: Representational Relativity named as public-facing principle
timeline.summary: Representational Relativity is named as a more legible umbrella principle: representations may vary while valid structure survives admissible transport.
constraints: Not the current canonical theory name.

timeline.title: Schemathematics crystallizes
timeline.summary: Schemas are differentiated as bounded representational forms carrying typed slots, relations, admissibility conditions, invariants, transformations, validation, defects, and repair. Schemathematics becomes the study of admissible construction, transformation, and closure of representational objects.
constraints: Current placement does not prove that every later Representational Mechanics concept was already present in the first Schemathematics formulation.

timeline.title: Second-Order Scientific Method origin-program package
timeline.summary: A comprehensive origin-program package joins the long-run GR/QFT problem, primitive representational questions, agentic pressure on fixed possibility spaces, Distinction Space, Contexture, the n-ball proto-schema, and the second-order scientific method.
constraints: Package date is a synthesis date, not proof that every mature term first appeared on 2026-08-01.

timeline.title: Earliest retained Schemathematics to Representational Mechanics checkpoint
timeline.summary: The earliest retained checkpoint records the historical relation in which Schemathematics supplies representational machinery to Representational Mechanics.
constraints: Both endpoints are repository-backed; the exact historical causal edge remains conversation-grounded.

timeline.title: Founder III / The Oathbound working note
timeline.summary: A working note names a third-founder mode centered on consequence fidelity and converting exceptional founder perception into durable institutional instruments.
constraints: Working doctrine in Smithy; not canonical until reviewed and reconciled with Core Identity.

timeline.title: Current Boundary Theory architecture becomes explicitly source-controlled
timeline.summary: Repository source reconciliation records the current architecture as Boundary Theory centered on Distinction Space, typed operational facets, Contexture as composable subspace, and Representational Mechanics as a subordinate discipline with Formal Grammars, Boundary First, and Corpus Forge.

Representational Mechanics -> applying/study discipline subordinate to Boundary Theory
Boundary First -> portable operational method rather than theory

sequence: Volumology — geometric / extent / region / interface emphasis
RGT — gauge-indexed representation / closure umbrella across mathematical and system representations
Distinction / Admissibility / Emergence + Contexture + invariants / transport / closure / defect / repair + Representational Relativity + Schemathematics
Boundary Theory — Distinction Space central object; typed facets; Contexture; Representational Mechanics; Formal Grammars; Boundary First; Corpus Forge
current_best_rgt_reconstruction.safe_historical_statement: RGT was an important intermediate umbrella in which the geometric intuitions of Volumology were generalized into a theory of representation, gauge, invariance, closure, defect, and cross-domain transport. The later Boundary Theory architecture did not merely rename RGT; it decomposed, retyped, and reorganized many of those concerns around Distinction Space, typed operational facets, Contexture, Representational Mechanics, and explicit formal apparatus. The exact repository-direct transition remains to be recovered.
forbidden_inferences: RGT was renamed Boundary Theory on a known date.
RGT is synonymous with Boundary Theory.
Volumology and RGT are identical programs.
Current architectural elegance proves the exact historical path.
